## Summary

[Partial] Remove the radiator to gain access for removing the crankshaft pulley. [t990]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the radiator to gain access for removing the crankshaft pulley.
2. Use a large air wrench (approx. 2-foot length) to knock loose and remove the stubborn crankshaft pulley.

_Procedure reported by [t990]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a large flat-tip screwdriver in the flywheel access panel for automatic 2x4s if lacking a special Nissan stopper. [t990]
- [Partial] Dip new parts in fresh oil before installation to ensure proper seating and reduce noise. [t990]
- Take lots of pictures during disassembly, especially timing marks on cams and crankshaft sprockets. [t990]
- Use drift pins inserted into large bolt holes to align the heavy front cover easily. [t990]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Failing to seat a cam sprocket fully in its hole before tightening bolts, causing it to spin and damage itself or other components during operation. [t990]
